warnings: Axes: x = 1-2-3 at 3.00 + 3.00 (6.00); y = A-B-C-D-E at 3.00 + 3.00 + 2.00 + 2.00 (10.00). Origin A1. The same main chains print on S-01, both S-02 views, S-03, S-04, A-07 (x) and A-08 (y). Vector CAD PDF with no usable text layer — every value read off the rendered page.

Two different ticks sit between 2 and 3 on the two floors: 4.30 (1.30 + 1.70, ground floor, S1/S2 bathroom split) and 4.20 (1.20 + 1.80, second floor and roof plan +6.30). They differ by 0.10 m, so they are two lines (2''' = 4.20, 2'''' = 4.30), not one edge printed twice.

Truss panel ticks on S-05 (T1/T2 every 1.00, T3 every 0.50, all along 1-3 = 6.00) became x dummies per section 4 rule 4; dummy names follow position order, which is why the beam-plan lines at 4.20/4.30 carry three and four primes.

Sweep scope (op04): structural sheets S-01..S-05 plus building sections A-07/A-08 (the only sheets printing levels). Architectural plans A-03/A-04, elevations A-05/A-06, stair/sanitary/electrical/plumbing sheets were not swept for dimensions — their chains are not in dimension_chains[]. A-09 (stair) was later read for the ST-01 stair section: its two chains (15@0.197 = 2.95 vertical, 0.98 + 0.85 = 1.83 horizontal) carry no grid marker or level label, so they stay on the ST-01 element. A-11 (door/window schedule) prints only element-internal opening dimensions, kept on its elements.

The S-06 footing-detail chains (0.18 + 0.18, 0.18 + 0.27 + 0.27 + 0.18, 1.00 / 0.50 / 0.05 / 0.05) and the PS detail dimensions are element-internal (section 4 rule 4 'not an axis tick') and stay on the elements.

dummy_grid_rule_check.negative_pos_m: x 1' (-1.00) and y A' (-1.00) sit before the origin (roof overhangs on S-04); 1' shares the 1 prime sequence with the truss ticks after grid 1 (1'' 0.50 ... 1'''''' 2.50).
